detailed_description: The Sunburst Chart Generator creates radial hierarchy charts that show parent-child relationships in a compact circular layout. It works well for category trees, budget structures, taxonomies, and other nested datasets where viewers need to understand both grouping and relative share. You can enter hierarchical labels and values, adjust colors, spacing, labels, and title settings, then export the result as PNG or SVG after reviewing the preview in the browser.
usage_steps: Enter the hierarchical labels and values you want to display, keeping parent-child relationships consistent.
Set the chart title and confirm the hierarchy reads from the center outward as intended.
Adjust colors, labels, and spacing so the nested rings remain clear.
Review the preview and refine the hierarchy if some branches feel too dense or unclear.
Export the completed sunburst chart as PNG or SVG for reports, docs, or presentations.
usage_examples: Show how a company budget breaks down from department to team to project level.
Visualize a content taxonomy so stakeholders can see the distribution of topics and subtopics.
Present a catalog structure with category, subcategory, and item-level share.

faqs.question: What is a sunburst chart best used for?
faqs.answer: A sunburst chart shows hierarchical parent-child relationships in concentric rings, ideal for budget trees, taxonomies, and category structures where both grouping and share matter.

faqs.question: What data format does the chart accept?
faqs.answer: The chart accepts hierarchical JSON with name, value, and children fields, so you can paste nested structures directly into the editor.

faqs.question: Can I adjust the ring thickness?
faqs.answer: Yes. You can tune the inner and outer radius settings to make the rings thicker or thinner and keep the chart readable.

faqs.question: Which export formats are available?
faqs.answer: You can export the rendered sunburst chart as high-resolution PNG or scalable vector SVG.
